requirement.original: Add semantic time constraints to timeline agent prompt so it doesn't put dinner at 17:10 and afternoon tea at 19:15
requirement.clarified: Add hard semantic time-window constraints to both the timeline agent definition (.claude/agents/timeline.md) and the Step 10 prompt in plan.md. Constraints must be enforced during timeline construction using the existing meal_ref tag, not post-hoc validation. Route optimisation for non-meal activities must remain unchanged.
requirement.what: Insert a semantic time-window constraint table and enforcement instruction into the timeline agent's scheduling logic in two files
requirement.why: Nearest-neighbor GPS optimisation ignores semantic meaning of meal types, producing absurd schedules (dinner at 17:10, afternoon tea at 19:15) that harm traveller experience
where: .claude/agents/timeline.md (Step 2: Create timeline dictionary and validation checklist)
.claude/commands/plan.md (Step 10 timeline agent prompt, Phase 2 Timeline Creation)

included: Hard time window constraints for breakfast, lunch, afternoon_tea/coffee, dinner
Constraint application via meal_ref tag (not name string matching)
entertainment entries with meal_ref inherit meal window
excluded: Changes to meals, entertainment, attractions, shopping agents
Changes to save.py, plan-validate.py, or any scripts
Configurable time windows from user preferences (deferred)
Auto-rescheduling of activities displaced by clamping

success_criteria: Dinner entry start_time is always >= 18:00 in generated timeline
Afternoon tea / coffee entry start_time is always <= 17:30
Breakfast entry start_time is always between 07:00 and 10:00
Lunch entry start_time is always between 11:30 and 14:00
Clamping events produce a warning in the day's warnings array
Non-meal activities (attractions, shopping) are unaffected by the change
meal_ref tag is the sole trigger for constraint application
constraints: Write tool is absolutely forbidden in timeline agent — constraints are enforced through prompt instructions only, no script changes
meal_ref schema tag already exists and is mandatory; new constraints must consume it, not re-derive meal type from names
Both files must be updated consistently; divergence between agent definition and Step 10 prompt would cause inconsistent behaviour depending on invocation path

root_cause_analysis.symptom: Dinner scheduled at 17:10 and afternoon matcha break scheduled at 19:15 in generated itinerary
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: The timeline agent's scheduling algorithm in Step 2 orders all activities (including meals) purely by GPS proximity using nearest-neighbor optimisation. There is no pre-scheduling constraint that pins meal activities to their semantically appropriate time windows before or during sequence construction. The existing 'verify meal times are reasonable' note appears only in the post-hoc validation checklist, not as an enforcement step during construction.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: N/A — design gap present from initial timeline agent creation; no single commit introduced the bug
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: Nearest-neighbor route optimisation was added to minimise total travel distance per day, which is a valid goal. At the time, meal time windows were listed only as a validation hint, not as a scheduling constraint, so the optimiser was free to place meals at any position in the sequence.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: GPS proximity optimisation has no concept of 'dinner should happen after 18:00'. When dinner is geographically close to an attraction that is naturally visited in the late afternoon, the optimiser places dinner immediately after that attraction — which may be as early as 17:00. This is semantically wrong and produces an itinerary that no real traveller would follow.
root_cause_analysis.timeline: Present from initial implementation; first reported concretely in this requirement

development_approach.strategy: Add a 'Semantic Time Windows' constraint block to the timeline construction instructions in both target files. The block defines five categories with their allowed start-time windows, instructs the agent to read meal_ref on each timeline entry and enforce the corresponding window, and requires a warning to be appended to the day warnings array when clamping occurs. Non-meal activities remain subject to proximity order only.

timeline_md: Step 2 'Create timeline dictionary' section — after the activity arrangement instruction, before the travel_segments section: insert SEMANTIC TIME WINDOW CONSTRAINTS block
Step 2 validation checklist bullet 'Verify meal times are reasonable (breakfast 7-10am, lunch 12-3pm, dinner 6-10pm)' — replace with reference to the new hard constraints block
plan_md: Step 10 Phase 2 Timeline Creation item 2 — after 'Schedule activities following route-optimization.json order for efficiency': insert the same SEMANTIC TIME WINDOW CONSTRAINTS block (condensed inline version)

afternoon_tea.trigger: meal_ref == afternoon_tea OR activity name contains tea/coffee/matcha without meal_ref (fallback)

development_approach.note_on_afternoon_tea: afternoon_tea is not a standard meal_ref value; the agent may need to detect it by activity name or by a future meal_ref value of 'afternoon_tea'. For now, instruct the agent to check for meal_ref == 'afternoon_tea' and also to pattern-match activity names containing 'tea', 'coffee', 'matcha', 'cafe' as a fallback. This is the one place where limited name-pattern matching is acceptable because there is no existing schema tag for this category.
development_approach.validation_approach: QA verifies by inspecting a generated timeline.json: dinner entries must have start_time >= 18:00, afternoon tea entries must have start_time <= 17:30, all meal entries must have a warning in the warnings array if their original proximity-optimal time fell outside their window.

research_findings.reason: Straightforward prompt-engineering fix with clear root cause: add time-window constraints to an existing scheduling instruction. The pattern (hard constraints + warning emission) is well-established in the codebase already (e.g., accommodation_ref, meal_ref enforcement). No new architecture or external patterns required.
